mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% interacts with a concurrent decline in personal income (PAYEMS) to signal a restrictive monetary policy that constrains both borrowing and demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a flat or declining GDP (GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average AND GDPC1 flat or declining for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.4 percentage points month-over-month signals a sharp labor market downturn, which immediately reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals broad-based contraction in the supply side of the economy, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both fall for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.
